title: Integer-window difference sieve for cyclic DCP

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the integer-window difference sieve with the single parameter choice in Section 5 of proof.md uses total work T(N,s) = O(2^(4 sqrt(n)) n^4) in the uniform Clifford+T bit-operation model of the challenge. All constants are absolute. The exact growth index of the displayed envelope is 1/2. This holds on every execution branch jointly with the other three resource bounds and unconditional full-secret recovery probability greater than 15/16 under the fifth claim, including the independent ideal source.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the integer-window difference sieve with the single parameter choice in Section 5 of proof.md uses peak classical memory S_C(N,s) = O(2^(2 sqrt(n)) n^(3/2)) bits. All constants are absolute. The exact growth index of the displayed envelope is 1/2. This holds on every execution branch jointly with the other three resource bounds and unconditional full-secret recovery probability greater than 15/16 under the fifth claim, including the independent ideal source.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the integer-window difference sieve with the single parameter choice in Section 5 of proof.md uses peak quantum memory S_Q(N,s) = O(2^(2 sqrt(n)) n^(1/2)) qubits. All constants are absolute. The exact growth index of the displayed envelope is 1/2. This holds on every execution branch jointly with the other three resource bounds and unconditional full-secret recovery probability greater than 15/16 under the fifth claim, including the independent ideal source.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the integer-window difference sieve with the single parameter choice in Section 5 of proof.md acquires at most eight copies for N=2 and at most (J+1) A_src + (2^(d+2)+1)(d+9) copies for n >= 2, counting every acquisition. Here b = ceil(2 sqrt(n)), d = ceil((n-2)/(b+1)), J = n-2-d, and A_src = 4*16^d*(2^b+262144(n+1)). Thus Q(N,s) = O(2^(4 sqrt(n)) n). All constants are absolute. The exact growth index of the displayed envelope is 1/2. This holds on every execution branch jointly with the other three resource bounds and unconditional full-secret recovery probability greater than 15/16 under the fifth claim, including the independent ideal source.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the integer-window difference sieve with the single parameter choice in Section 5 of proof.md guarantees the malformed-sample fraction epsilon(n) = 1 in the following source model. Before the run, the source may designate any fixed set of acquisition positions as malformed. Conditional on a jointly drawn vector of offsets in Z/NZ, all copies are a tensor product of pure coset states with the same shift s and the respective offsets. At honest positions the offsets are mutually independent uniform draws. At malformed positions the offsets may have any joint classical distribution, including dependence on s and on honest offsets. The joint draw is independent of the algorithm's private measurement outcomes. Each copy has the usual plus relative phase and the prescribed register dimensions. For any such choices, including when all acquisitions are designated malformed or when all are ideal, full-secret recovery succeeds with unconditional probability greater than 15/16 jointly with the four resource bounds.
